plants.name: Mistletoe cactus
plants.looks: Thin, hanging pencil-like stems with no spines.
plants.care: A jungle cactus that needs the most water of anything you have. Water when the top half of the soil is dry. Strong light burns it. Mix some orchid bark into its soil.
plants.thirsty: Stems look thin, dull or limp, and may wrinkle lengthwise. Healthy stems are plump and springy.

plants.name: Blue chalksticks
plants.looks: Blue-grey finger leaves pointing straight up.
plants.care: Grows in winter and wrinkles when it's thirsty. It can go semi-dormant in hot summer, so water less if it stops growing.
plants.thirsty: Its 'fingers' wrinkle lengthwise and lose their plumpness, and the blue color gets duller.

plants.name: Ripple jade
plants.looks: Wavy blue-grey leaves on a woody stem.
plants.care: Easygoing. Water when the soil is dry, and its leaves get a red edge in strong light.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and wrinkle a little, especially the older ones, and may droop slightly.

plants.name: Coppertone stonecrop
plants.looks: Pointed leaves with copper-orange tips.
plants.care: The orange color comes from strong light. If it turns green and stretches, move it closer to the bars.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and slightly shriveled, and the copper tips may look dull.

plants.name: Echeveria purpusorum (green)
plants.looks: Thick, sharp, pointed green rosette.
plants.care: Skip watering if the leaves still feel firm. Echeverias rot more easily than most of your plants. Use about a third pumice in the soil.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and slightly bendy instead of firm. The lower leaves wrinkle or deflate, and the rosette may close up a bit.

plants.name: Echeveria purpusorum (red)
plants.looks: Thick, sharp, pointed dark red rosette.
plants.care: Skip watering if the leaves still feel firm. Strong light keeps the deep red color.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and slightly bendy instead of firm. The lower leaves wrinkle or deflate, and the rosette may close up a bit.

plants.name: Echeveria 'Lola'
plants.looks: Smooth, pale lavender-grey rosette.
plants.care: Skip watering if the leaves still feel firm. Don't touch the leaves, because the powdery coating rubs off.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and slightly bendy instead of firm. The lower leaves wrinkle or deflate, and the rosette may close up a bit.

plants.name: Pachyveria 'Glauca'
plants.looks: Chunky blue-grey leaves like fat fingers, in a loose rosette.
plants.care: Skip watering if the leaves still feel firm. Use about a third pumice in the soil.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and slightly bendy instead of firm. The lower leaves wrinkle or deflate, and the rosette may close up a bit.

plants.name: Echeveria 'Neon Breaker'
plants.looks: Flat blue-green rosette with ruffled, pink-edged leaves.
plants.care: Its leaves are thinner than most Echeverias, so it drinks a little more. Give it a top spot under 2 strips, because strong light brings out the pink. You can separate the small pups at the base once they're about 1in across.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and slightly bendy instead of firm. The lower leaves wrinkle or deflate, and the rosette may close up a bit.

plants.name: Christmas carol aloe A
plants.looks: Spotted green leaves with red edges and bumps, growing low.
plants.care: Water when the soil is fully dry. Strong light keeps the red spots bright. Light: very flexible. Under 2 strips at any distance, a skylight or a sunny window are all fine; brighter light gives stronger red color. Only dim spots (gooseneck, dark corners) are a problem: it stretches and fades. Ease it into a hot south or west window to avoid sunburn.
plants.thirsty: Leaves thin out, curl inward and may wrinkle or feel soft. The tips can turn brown and crispy.

plants.name: Christmas carol aloe B
plants.looks: Spiky, upright aloe with speckled leaves.
plants.care: Water when the soil is fully dry. It may be the Purple People Eater aloe from Planet Desert. Light: very flexible. Under 2 strips at any distance, a skylight or a sunny window are all fine; brighter light gives stronger red color. Only dim spots (gooseneck, dark corners) are a problem: it stretches and fades. Ease it into a hot south or west window to avoid sunburn.
plants.thirsty: Leaves thin out, curl inward and may wrinkle or feel soft. The tips can turn brown and crispy.

plants.name: Corn cob (terracotta)
plants.looks: A single bumpy cream-and-green column, like a corn cob.
plants.care: Its white sap irritates skin and eyes and is toxic to dogs. Use about 50% pumice in the soil.
plants.thirsty: The column looks slightly shrunken or wrinkled between the bumps or ribs, and it feels less firm.

plants.name: Corn cob (blue pot)
plants.looks: A clump of tall, bumpy cream-and-green columns.
plants.care: Same care as the terracotta corn cob. If the columns lean toward the light, rotate the pot every week.
plants.thirsty: The column looks slightly shrunken or wrinkled between the bumps or ribs, and it feels less firm.

plants.name: Euphorbia spiralis
plants.looks: A ribbed column that twists in a spiral.
plants.care: New from Planet Desert. Its sap is toxic to dogs. Use gritty soil.
plants.thirsty: The column looks slightly shrunken or wrinkled between the bumps or ribs, and it feels less firm.

plants.name: Green Coral
plants.looks: A crested, fan-shaped mound of tiny green fingers.
plants.care: New arrival. Crested forms rot if they stay wet, so water around the crest, not on it.
plants.thirsty: The crest looks thinner, softer and slightly wrinkled. Water around it, not on it.

plants.name: Euphorbia enopla
plants.looks: A spiny column with bright red spines.
plants.care: New arrival. Strong light keeps the spines red. Its sap is toxic to dogs.
plants.thirsty: The column looks slightly shrunken or wrinkled between the bumps or ribs, and it feels less firm.

plants.name: Euphorbia stenoclada (spineless)
plants.looks: Branching silver-green stems, like coral.
plants.care: New arrival. Tough and forgiving. Its sap is toxic to dogs.
plants.thirsty: Stems look skinnier and slightly wrinkled. Thirsty plants may drop their small leaves.

plants.name: African milk tree
plants.looks: Tall, three-sided stems tinged red, with small leaves.
plants.care: New arrival. It handles medium light well. Rotate it so it grows straight.
plants.thirsty: Leaves droop or drop, and the three-sided stems look a little wrinkled or soft.

plants.name: Coral cactus
plants.looks: A wavy, crested fan, often grafted onto a stem.
plants.care: New arrival. Give it medium light, at the edge of the bars or in the skylight room. Keep water off the crest.
plants.thirsty: The crest looks thinner, softer and slightly wrinkled. Water around it, not on it.

plants.name: Firesticks
plants.looks: Smooth pencil stems that turn orange-red.
plants.care: New arrival. It only turns red in strong light. Its sap is especially irritating, so wear gloves when you handle it.
plants.thirsty: Stems look skinnier and slightly wrinkled. Thirsty plants may drop their small leaves.

plants.name: Hobbit jade
plants.looks: Tube-shaped leaves with suction-cup-like tips.
plants.care: New arrival. It's easy to grow, and its leaf tips turn red in strong light.
plants.thirsty: Leaves feel soft and wrinkle a little, especially the older ones, and may droop slightly.

plants.name: Monkey's Tail
plants.looks: A trailing stem covered in soft white hair.
plants.care: Give it lots of light. The hairs are soft, but there are spines underneath.
plants.thirsty: The stem looks slightly shrunken or wrinkled near the base and feels less firm.

plants.name: Lifesaver plant
plants.looks: Toothy green stems. Its flowers look like striped donuts.
plants.care: Too much light turns it red and stressed. It's the most rot-prone plant you have, so use about 50% pumice and keep it fairly dry in winter.
plants.thirsty: Stems wrinkle and look a little deflated or soft. Firm, plump stems are well-watered.

plants.name: Inchworm
plants.looks: Grey-green stems with dark stripes that arch over and root where they touch the soil.
plants.care: It's recovering from root rot. Keep it dry for 1–2 weeks after repotting and in medium light until it re-roots, then move it under the bars. Keep it on the dry side in winter.
plants.thirsty: Stems wrinkle and look a little deflated or soft. Firm, plump stems are well-watered.

plants.name: Fairy washboard
plants.looks: A small, stiff, dark green rosette with raised ridges across the leaves, like a washboard.
plants.care: It likes softer light than most of your plants, so the skylight room is ideal. Glazed pots dry slowly, so check the soil first. Water less in midsummer.
plants.thirsty: Leaves thin, curl inward and lose their plumpness, and the leaf tips may brown.

plants.name: Millot kalanchoe
plants.looks: Soft, fuzzy, pale green round leaves with scalloped edges.
plants.care: Water the soil, not the fuzzy leaves. It's toxic to dogs. If it gets leggy, pinch the stem tips; the cuttings root easily.
plants.thirsty: Fuzzy leaves feel soft and floppy and may curl, and the plant can droop.

plants.name: Prickly pears (all)
plants.looks: Flat, paddle-shaped pads.
plants.care: Watch out for glochids, the tiny hair-like spines, and handle them with tongs or gloves. Water lightly in winter.
plants.thirsty: The pads wrinkle, look thinner and may lean or sag.

plants.name: Thumb cactus
plants.looks: A small, finger-shaped cactus.
plants.care: Keep it mostly dry in winter. Use about 50% pumice in the soil.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Rebutia heliosa
plants.looks: A tiny ball covered in neat, comb-like silver spines.
plants.care: Keep it dry through winter so it flowers in spring, and give it a light first watering in March.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Chin cactus / "Ruby Ball"
plants.looks: A small, dark green, ribbed ball with a bump under each spine cluster, like a chin.
plants.care: It needs less light than most cacti: 1 strip at about 8in is ideal. Too much light turns it red-brown or bleached, so move it back if that happens; if it stretches, move it closer. Keep it nearly dry in winter.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Mother of hundreds
plants.looks: A pale green ball covered in neat angular bumps with short spines. It clusters into a big mound over time, which is how it got its name.
plants.care: One of the easiest. It flowers pink in spring after a cool, dry winter.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Ruby Ball #2
plants.looks: A dark green, ribbed ball with pale spine clusters and chin-like bumps. It's the second one, from the sampler box.
plants.care: Same care as your other Ruby Ball: 1 strip at about 8in, and nearly dry in winter. Too much light turns it red-brown.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Green tomato cactus
plants.looks: A dark green, flattened ball with bumpy ribs and curved, pale spines.
plants.care: Big yellow flowers in spring. Keep it dry in winter, and it likes the strongest light.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Horse crippler
plants.looks: A low, dark green dome with a few broad ribs and very stiff, thick spines, some curved down.
plants.care: Its spines are seriously stiff, so keep it well away from paws and noses. Give it full light and very little water in winter. It's native to Texas and New Mexico.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Tobusch fishhook cactus
plants.looks: A small ball covered in long, hooked, fishhook-like spines.
plants.care: The fussiest cactus you have. It rots easily, so use very gritty soil (at least 50% pumice) and water sparingly, even in summer. Skip watering if there's any doubt.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Brasilicactus (Scarlet ball)
plants.looks: A ball densely covered in fine, golden-white hair-like spines, often tilting toward the light.
plants.care: Flowers in late winter or early spring after a cool, dry rest. Rotate it so it doesn't lean.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Chin cactus (anisitsii)
plants.looks: A dark green, ribbed column-like ball with chin bumps and long pale spines. Yours has a pup growing on top.
plants.care: Give it medium light, like the Ruby Balls. You can remove the pup once it's about a third of the parent's size; let it dry a few days, then pot it up.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

plants.name: Scarlet hedgehog cactus
plants.looks: A short, spiny green column with dense grey-and-brown spines. It forms clumps over time.
plants.care: A New Mexico native and the most cold-hardy plant you own. It flowers bright red in spring if it gets a cold, dry winter and strong light.
plants.thirsty: The stem looks slightly shrunken or wrinkled near the base and feels less firm.

plants.name: Rainbow pincushion
plants.looks: A bright green ball of spiraling bumps (no ribs), each with a star of golden-yellow spines and a little white wool. New spines often come in reddish, which gives the 'rainbow' bands.
plants.care: From the Planet Desert 9-pack. Easy. Give it strong light, gritty soil and a cool, dry winter, and it rewards you with a ring of magenta flowers around the top in spring.
plants.thirsty: The body shrinks and looks slightly wrinkled or puckered, and the ribs or bumps look deeper. It feels softer when you squeeze it gently.

tips.golden_rule: Only water when the soil is fully dry. Soak until water runs out of the drainage hole, then let it drain. When in doubt, wait.
signs: Stretching or pale new growth: it needs more light
Red or purple blush at the tips: mild light stress, usually fine
Pale, washed-out patches after 1–2 weeks: bleaching, so back off the light
Wrinkled or soft leaves: it's thirsty
Mushy, translucent or black spots: too much water or rot
tips.lights: Run the lights 12–14 hours a day on a timer. Ease new plants in by starting them 12–14in from the bars, or running the lights 8–10 hours a day, for 1–2 weeks.
tips.soil: Mix pumice into bagged succulent mix: about 50% for plants with high rot risk, about a third for medium risk. Plants with low risk are fine in plain mix.
tips.new_arrivals: Unbox right away and check for cold damage. Don't water on arrival. Repot into dry soil, wait about a week, then water on the plant's next block night.
tips.root_rot: Cut back to firm tissue, let the cuts dry for a few days, repot into dry gritty mix, and wait 1–2 weeks before a light watering. Give it medium light until it re-roots.
tips.dogs: Keep these up high: all Euphorbias (corn cobs, spiralis, Green Coral, enopla, stenoclada, African milk tree, Coral cactus, and especially Firesticks) and the Millot kalanchoe. Up high is also best for the aloes, jades, Blue chalksticks and Inchworm, which are mildly toxic and usually cause vomiting or drooling. The cacti aren't poisonous, but their spines and glochids hurt mouths and paws. Safe at floor level: the Echeverias, Lola, Pachyveria, Neon Breaker, Coppertone, Fairy washboard, Mistletoe cactus and Lifesaver. If a dog chews something, call your vet or the ASPCA Animal Poison Control line, (888) 426-4435.
tips.cold_signs: Mild cold stress: red, purple or bronze tint, or slight shriveling, which is harmless. Cold damage: glassy, translucent or water-soaked spots, usually on the side facing the window or at the tips and new growth. These go soft and mushy, then brown or black, or later dry into tan, corky scars. Check by pressing gently: firm is fine, soft means damage. If you see damage, move the plant somewhere warmer, keep it dry and wait a few days to see how far it spreads. Then cut out any mushy tissue back to firm, clean flesh and let it dry. A cheap min/max thermometer on the sill shows how cold it really gets at night.
tips.pests: Mealybugs look like white cotton tufts in crevices, spine clusters and at the base. Dab each one with a cotton swab dipped in 70% isopropyl alcohol, or mist the plant with alcohol (or alcohol mixed 1:1 with water and a drop of dish soap). Test a small spot first, and keep the plant out of strong light for a day afterward. Repeat every 5 to 7 days for about 4 weeks, because eggs keep hatching. Isolate the plant while you treat it. If it keeps coming back, unpot it and check the roots for white fuzz (root mealybugs), then rinse them and repot in fresh dry soil.
tips.thirsty_note: Thirst signs are a nudge, not an emergency: water at the next block night, or sooner if it's bad. Mushy, translucent or yellowing parts mean the opposite, too much water, so stop watering and let the plant dry out.

window_key.ok: OK on the NE sill (less color)
